memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: then her first husband, who divorced her, is not allowed to marry her again after she has been defiled. That would be detestable in the eyes of the Lord. Do not bring sin upon the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance. - Deut 24:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse completes the case begun before, once a woman had divorced and remarried, her first husband could not take her back again. While the details feel foreign to us, the law served to protect against treating marriage and people carelessly, as though relationships could be casually broken and re-formed at will. It placed a serious limit that guarded the dignity of marriage and discouraged people from treating a spouse as disposable.

Behind this regulation lies God's concern that His people not sin against the sanctity of marriage or bring guilt upon the land. Even in dealing with the sad reality of divorce, God was upholding the seriousness and dignity of the marriage covenant. Relationships were not toys to be picked up and discarded and picked up again.

The deeper truth for us is that God takes covenant relationships seriously, far more seriously than our casual culture often does. He calls His people to honour their commitments and to treat marriage as sacred. This points us to God's own covenant faithfulness. Unlike our wavering hearts, God never treats His people as disposable. In Christ, He has made an unbreakable covenant of love with us, one He will never abandon (Heb 13:5). His steadfast faithfulness is the model for how we are to value our own commitments. How can you reflect God's covenant faithfulness in the relationships He has given you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you treat your commitments as seriously as God does?
2. How does God's unbreakable covenant love encourage you?
3. Where can you show greater faithfulness in your relationships?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You never treat me as disposable but keep covenant with me forever. Help me honour my commitments faithfully, reflecting You. Amen.
